title: voice-lint.mjs: the Stop-hook voice obligation is scoped to the turn that produced the record (turn boundary + residuals i-ix)
content:
Landed at #56, squash-merged to main as b5f6f52 (PR #87; source range starts at 8436ecf, ends 4429ab2 -- re-derive with `git log --oneline 8436ecf^..4429ab2` on a checkout with the source branch, or `git show b5f6f52 --stat`). Fixes plugins/pipeline/scripts/voice-lint.mjs, no other file. This was a 3-round Phase 2 (SecOps VETO + DBA REQUEST_CHANGES round 1, both closed round 2 with a new blocker, fully closed round 3), a Phase 2.5 design bake-off, a 6-agent Phase 4 panel with one delta round, then a text-only precision pass. Final: 12 requirements, 18 acceptance criteria, 267 test cells in test-voice-lint.sh (up from 71 pre-#56).

THE DEFECT voice-lint fixed. Before #56, run() decided whether to impose voice.md's shape from ONE input: current_phase of whichever .pipeline/<issue>/status.json is newest by mtime. That carries no notion of WHEN (a terminal phase like 5-archived states a true fact forever, so every later message in the session got graded as the completion report -- the in-run half) and no notion of WHOSE (when the current run's record is REMOVED at archival, the mtime scan falls through to some OTHER lane's parked record and grades this session's message against a run it does not own -- the cross-run half, reproduced live during this issue's own Phase 2 rounds).

THE FIX, as an outcome property: no message can be refused on account of a status record that has not been touched since the last OWNER-AUTHORED turn began. Nothing is remembered; both the record's freshness and the turn boundary are DERIVED each invocation from inputs the Stop hook already has (the transcript path, the resolved status record's mtime and updated_at). The predicate is phase-independent, so 5-archived, halted-error and the whole <phase>-error family inherit it for free.

MECHANISM (voice-lint.mjs, current shape). resolveStatus(projectDir, envIssue) now returns { status, dir, mtimeMs } | null instead of a bare parsed record (precedence, the strict-newest-mtime scan and the tie-abstention on exact-mtime collisions are UNCHANGED -- R4 froze that behaviour deliberately; see architecture--status-schema-json-consumers.json's sibling AC9 divergence table against validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's activeIssueDir, which is NOT a mirror, just a superficially similar independent derivation). lastAssistantText was renamed scanTranscript(transcriptPath) and returns { text, humanTurnMs } out of the SAME single reverse loop the file already ran, so no second transcript read is added (R12). isHumanTurnRecord(record) is a new, EXPORTED, six-clause ANDed positive-provenance predicate: record.type === 'user', record.isSidechain !== true, record.isMeta !== true, record.message?.role === 'user', record.origin?.kind === 'human', and Date.parse(record.timestamp) finite. recordFreshnessMs(mtimeMs, updatedAt) = Math.max(mtimeMs, Date.parse(updatedAt) when finite, else mtimeMs). run() gains exactly one new conditional block after the existing empty-text return: if a human turn boundary was found AND the resolved record's freshness is older than that boundary, return { failures: [], phase } (silence). main() gains exactly one conditional line, outside failures.map, naming when no human turn was resolvable at all (R10), so a permanent no-op degradation is visible rather than looking identical to the control working.

THE ORIGIN.KIND NESTING HAZARD -- the single most consequential implementation detail in this fix, worth its own paragraph because it is a FATAL, SILENT misreading trap. `origin` is a RECORD-LEVEL field in Claude Code transcript JSONL, a SIBLING of type/isSidechain/isMeta/timestamp/message -- it is NEVER message.origin. Measured over the full corpus at spec time: 2,742 record-level origin objects (2,391 main-session + 351 subagent), ZERO under message, in any observed client version (2.1.85 through 2.1.237). The correct access is record.origin?.kind; record.message?.origin?.kind is the natural misreading (origin.kind is listed immediately after message.role in the predicate's clause order and shares its rhythm) and it is CATASTROPHIC if shipped: it finds ZERO human turns on every transcript ever written, so the freshness-silencing branch never fires, R3's louder-fallback always applies, and the fix ships as a PERMANENT, TOTAL, SILENT no-op that is behaviourally indistinguishable from the control working. A generic vendor-drift mutation battery CANNOT catch this (a permanently-loud predicate trivially passes every drift cell, since loud is what those cells assert) -- only a dedicated nesting-discrimination PAIR catches it: a captured owner record with origin correctly placed (must exit 2 at a stale-record boundary) against the same record with origin RELOCATED under message (must ALSO exit 2, because a relocated origin is not a recognised human turn under the correct implementation, but WOULD read as 2 under the wrong-message-nested implementation too via a different, silently-broken path -- the pair inverts BOTH cells at once under the bug). If you are implementing ANY predicate over Claude Code transcript records that reads a field named similarly to origin/message, verify the nesting level against a live transcript before shipping, and add a discrimination pair, not just a positive fixture.

WHY origin.kind over exclusion-based classification. The pre-#56 round-1 attempt at this same fix (never merged) defined a human turn by EXCLUDING known machine record shapes rather than positively identifying owner records, and every excluded-by-default record therefore silently qualified as a human turn: this included voice-lint's OWN Stop-hook refusal record (AC13's self-disarm: the control disarmed itself on first fire, so a resent identical bad message passed on resend -- SecOps's VETO), background task-completion notices (1,377 of 1,377 measured), auto-compaction continuations (DBA's second blocker), and cross-session messages from another process on the same machine. origin.kind is the vendor's own provenance label and discriminates all of these directly: task-notification records carry origin.kind 'task-notification' (100% of 1,377, zero absent-origin exceptions across all client versions observed, including old ones); cross-session peer messages carry origin.kind 'peer' AND isMeta true (excluded twice over, since sessionId cannot see them -- all 31 observed carry the RECEIVING session's own id); voice-lint's own refusal records and auto-compaction summaries carry NO origin field at all and are excluded by the positive-origin requirement (the refusal record is additionally excluded by isMeta true). isSidechain and isMeta are kept even though origin.kind alone would already exclude every observed instance of what they guard, because they cost nothing, only ever narrow (narrower is louder, which is the safe direction for this predicate), and give the cross-session class a second independent exclusion.

THE GENERALISABLE RULE for any future 'has a person weighed in' predicate over a shared record stream the harness also writes to: identify the class you want POSITIVELY, never by subtracting the classes you happen to have enumerated -- a future vendor-added record shape inherits inclusion under exclusion-based logic and exclusion under positive-identification logic, and only the second direction is safe for a control whose failure mode is silence.

DECLARED RESIDUALS (module header, voice-lint.mjs, current as of b5f6f52), each with its FAIL DIRECTION and its EXPIRY, in label order i through ix. Full text lives in the module header itself (`git show b5f6f52:plugins/pipeline/scripts/voice-lint.mjs | sed -n '1,150p'` approximately, re-derive line numbers by grepping 'RESIDUAL' in the file) -- summarised here so a future reader does not have to reconstruct the reasoning from the spec: (i) a mid-turn git checkout/clone/worktree-add/sync that rewrites a FOREIGN status.json's mtime can make it look fresh and capture the turn -- FALSE REFUSAL, today's behaviour, unmitigated. (ii) an owner message between the archive checkpoint and the completion report ends the turn before the report -- SILENCE, the one true positive this fix accepts as a trade. (iii-a) an mtime moved backwards (NTP step, explicit utimes) on freshly-written bytes is bounded by max(mtime, updated_at) reading fresh -- LOUD, closed by R9's max() composition. (iii-b) OPEN and UNCLOSED: an mtime-PRESERVING restore (cp -p, rsync -a, tar -x) carries the stale updated_at along with the stale mtime, so BOTH terms of max() read stale together and the record silences even though it was placed this turn -- SILENCE, a DECLARED residual (see the decisions/declared-bounded-residual-over-forced-mechanical-fix.json record for the pattern this exemplifies), measured zero occurrences of cp -p/rsync/tar anywhere under plugins/ or .github/ at spec time, pinned by AC16(d) with its own expiry written into the test assertion message. (iv) IRREDUCIBLE: the predicate trusts the vendor's own origin.kind label; if a future client stamps a harness-injected record origin.kind 'human', that record silently becomes a human turn. Declared expected survivor, not mitigated; expiry is re-running the origin.kind census on a fresh corpus. (v) same-machine cross-session messages, excluded twice over (origin.kind 'peer' + isMeta true; sessionId is NOT a usable third guard, ruled out with its measurement). (vi) clients predating the origin field (8 of 84 transcripts, 9.5%, all 2.1.170 or older) resolve no human turn at all -- LOUD NO-OP, today's behaviour, made visible by R10's fixed stderr line rather than silently degrading. (vii) a turn the owner did not START (auto-compaction continuation, task-notification handoff, session resume, cross-session peer) does not advance the boundary, so an archived record inside the window between a status write and the next owner-typed message still reads fresh and gets graded -- FALSE REFUSAL, a bounded coverage limit, NOT the whole of the original in-run problem. (viii) FOUND AT PHASE 2.5 by the design-bake-off judge, in NEITHER of the two competing sketches: phaseShapeFailure refuses BEFORE the transcript is even read, so a stale/foreign record with a malformed current_phase still refuses this session's message regardless of turn scoping -- FALSE REFUSAL, a coverage limit, not moved earlier deliberately (moving the freshness check above the shape check would make the shape-failure path pay a transcript read it does not pay today). (ix) FOUND AT PHASE 4 by DBA: a stat failure on resolveStatus's explicit-signal branch (a new statSync call this fix introduces) is guarded to return mtimeMs = +Infinity on throw so a tooling failure can only read maximally fresh and never silence -- but the ORIGINAL scope of this guard's rationale named only the statSync catch and missed that existsSync at a sibling call site reaches the identical silent-drop outcome for the same persistent-permission-fault scenario; both sites are now named together in the final text-only fix (d7455bc/1245f03/4429ab2).

R12 (single transcript read per invocation) and R11 (the new human-turn scan must never reach main()'s blanket fail-open try/catch at voice-lint.mjs's tail, which is the same #61 defect class DevOps flagged against the sibling gate-phase-entry.mjs module) both hold structurally in the shipped code, not by convention -- the human-turn scan is fused into the SAME reverse loop scanTranscript already ran, and every one of its six field accesses is a per-record optional-chain guard that treats a malformed record as NOT a human turn rather than throwing.

A follow-up tracker issue (#91) carries five non-blocking items surfaced during review: residual (viii) not yet listed in spec.json's own R7 prose (a spec/code documentation gap, not a code gap); a tie-direction asymmetry and a fallback return-shape change with an expiring safety premise (both small internal inconsistencies); two test-harness observability nits (run.sh not naming which suite failed; a git-clone-blindness hazard in an integration test, see testing--voice-lint-fixture-capture-and-mutation-discipline.json); and minor hygiene (a hardcoded path in a test fixture script, stale line-number citations in comments).
